question.text: This "Commodore" made his initial money in the shipping industry, but later made his fortune in the railroad industry. He is also the namesake of a Tennessee university.
question.clue: During the California Gold Rush, this person created the Accessory Transit Company to bring passengers from the East Coast to San Francisco via Nicaragua.

swap.leadin: A "southern" version of this structure was made through the Gadsden Purchase in present-day New Mexico and Arizona.
swap.text: Name this structure constructed in the 1860s which extended from San Francisco Bay to Council Bluffs, Iowa.
swap.clue: This entity was financed by the Big Four, which included Leland Stanford.

question.leadin: Eugene Debs was arrested in the aftermath of this event, after which he became a Socialist.
question.text: Name this railroad strike and boycott that crippled transportation in 1894.
question.clue: General Nelson Miles was sent to put down this event on the order of Richard Olney, in the name of protecting mail shipments.

swap.text: Bryan lost the 1896 Presidential election after being heavily outspent by this man. He was succeeded by Theodore Roosevelt after his 1901 assassination in Buffalo, New York.
swap.clue: He was criticized for his nomination of the possibly senile John Sherman to Secretary of State.

question.text: The so-called "embalmed" beef scandal occurred in the U.S. Army during this conflict. The Insular Cases concerned American territorial gains from this war, such as Guam.
question.clue: William Randolph Hearst's "yellow journalism" inflamed support for this conflict after the explosion of the Maine.

swap.text: The treasury was also required to purchase silver by this 1878 act which reinstated silver as legal tender and created a policy of bimetallism.
swap.clue: It replaced the "Crime of 1873" and mandated a 16-to-1 ratio after it was passed over the veto of Rutherford B. Hayes, who only complied with the minimum requirements of this law.

question.text: Commodore George Dewey, "You may fire when ready, Gridley."
question.clue: The fighting took place around Sangley Point and commenced with the enemy's abandonment of its flagship, the Queen Christina.

swap.text: The Homestead steel works had been bought by this Scottish steel magnate who also wrote "The Gospel of Wealth" and founded a university in Pittsburgh.
swap.clue: His works include Round the World and Triumphant Democracy.

question.leadin: Answer the following about some influential political cartoons in American history.
question.text: An early color cartoon from Puck magazine lampooned this presidential candidate as the "tattooed man" whose body was covered in a sea of scandals. His namesake amendments barred government funding for parochial schools.
question.clue: He tried to mollify the American response to the USS Baltimore incident using contacts he made as chair of the first Pan-American Conference.

swap.leadin: Secretary of the Treasury Abel Corbin attempted to end it by releasing some of the federal gold reserve.
swap.text: What was this September 24, 1869 event, the culmination of two speculators' attempt to corner the gold market, which drove the price up to $13.50 an ounce?
swap.clue: An important participant was Abel Corbin, who brought the architects of this scheme into high social circles.

question.text: This man was impeached as Secretary of War after it was revealed he took bribes to influence his apportionment of trading posts in Oklahoma.
question.clue: This Secretary of War under Grant was forced to resign after receiving bribes for post tradership positions. He's the only cabinet secretary to ever have been impeached.

swap.text: This author wrote King Leopold's Soliloquy, a satirical criticism of Leopold's policy towards the Congo. This American author wrote about his tour of the Middle East in The Innocents Abroad.
swap.clue: This author and unscrupulous investor who invented an unsuccessful memory game while procrastinating on writing The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn.

question.text: John F. Stevens surveyed Montana for this railway led by James J. Hill, whose route crossed Marias Pass and Glacier National Park. Amtrak now operates this former competitor of Northern Pacific with a mountain goat logo.
question.answerHtml: Great Northern Railway [or GN; accept Empire Builder; accept Burlington Northern and Santa Fe or or BNSF]

swap.leadin: It passed the Sherman Antitrust and Silver Purchase Acts and raised the average tariff rate to 48.4% with the McKinley Tariff.
swap.text: Name this Congress, nicknamed for its supposed overspending.
swap.clue: This U.S. Congress whose lavish spending earned it a derisive nickname.

question.leadin: Public outrage over this practice in New York City led to a 1788 riot during which John Jay was reportedly hit over the head with a rock.
question.text: Name this practice that inspired the passage of "bone bills" in several states, as introduced by the president of the American Chemical Society, John William Draper.
question.answerHtml: body snatching [accept equivalents like stealing corpses or digging up bodies; or cadaver research; prompt on grave robbing or stealing by asking “what objects were stolen?”]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about various structures named Stone Bridge.
swap.text: At least 80 people were killed when the Stone Bridge caught on fire during this disaster. Because Philander Knox argued that this disaster was an Act of God, the South Fork Fishing and Hunting Club paid no damages.
swap.clue: This event was made worse when a fire broke out on the Stone Bridge.

question.text: John Henry Manny initially hired Lincoln, then replaced him with Edwin Stanton, to deliver the closing statement in a patent case centered on this device. The inventor of this device founded a company that eventually developed into the IHC.
question.answerHtml: mechanical reaper [or reaping machine] (The inventor of the reaper was Cyrus McCormick.)
question.clue: This device created by Cyrus McCormick that used a horse-drawn frame with rapidly moving blades to efficiently cut through grain.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a nosy postal inspector.
swap.text: This founder of the Society for the Suppression of Vice is best known for supporting a namesake 1873 law banning the sending of obscene materials through the US mail service.
swap.clue: This man raised funds to purchase the printing press of William Hayes, a surgeon he had driven to suicide.

question.leadin: Identify the following regarding the history of the Mormon movement, FTPE.
question.text: The Supreme Court ruled that religious practices were not exempt from the authority of federal law in this 1879 case involving the eponymous Mormon polygamist.
question.clue: The Poland Act led to this 1878 test case, with a majority written by Chief Justice Morrison Waite. The Church allowed a man to be charged with bigamy; the Court upheld laws against polygamy against the argument that they infringed upon religious duty.

swap.leadin: He dropped out of consideration for the democratic ticket in the election of 1900 after claiming the president's job was simply following orders from congress.
swap.text: Name this man who was the sole Admiral of the Navy and led the American fleet at the Battle of Manilla Bay.
swap.clue: This man annihilated the fleet of Patricio Montojo y Pasaron by issuing the order "You may fire when you are ready, Gridley" while on board his flagship, the USS Olympia.
